title: Lineage V foundational body plan
scope: Lineage-level body plan of Lineage V, the tri-radial hydrostatic lineage, distinguishing its ancestral core from the family-care migrant's derived specialisations; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Lineage V bodies are organised on tri-radial symmetry rather than the bilateral symmetry of Lineages I, III, and IV.
Support and movement are hydrostatic: pressurised internal fluid working against flexible tissue, with no rigid internal skeleton and no exoskeleton.
Travelling waves passing along body margins are a basic lineage-wide movement mode.

The family-care migrant's low three-lobed vault silhouette, ring of short paddle-columns, underside refuge, and shelter–forage–regroup care system are derived and branch-specific rather than lineage-wide.
The family-care migrant is one specialised caregiving member of the lineage, and its own records continue to govern it unchanged.
boundaries: Tri-radial, hydrostatic, and margin wave are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The plan establishes no cnidarian, echinoderm, worm, or other Earth-clade homology and no direct Earth-animal transplant.

Tri-radial symmetry describes qualitative body organisation; it establishes no perfect symmetry, fixed angles, three of any organ, three identities, or invariant external form, and derived branches may be secondarily asymmetric.

Hydrostatic support establishes a mechanical principle, not exact fluid, chambering, pressure, valves, musculature, control, or performance, and it does not preclude local stiffening tissues short of a rigid skeleton.

Travelling margin waves establish local tissue motion contributing to movement, not environmental waves, Mana pulses, sonar, signalling, an aura, group control, or a specialised ability; their actuation, speed, and efficiency remain open, and the family-care migrant's bounded outlet-passage sequence remains governed by its own record.
Predominantly aquatic is qualitative; whether any branch is fully terrestrial, amphibious, sessile, or colonial remains open, as do desiccation and freezing tolerances.
Body-wall breaches are mechanically serious for hydrostatic bodies as a structural tendency; no wound threshold, healing rate, or mortality outcome is established.

Which branches, if any, carry vaults, paddle-columns, underside refuges, or parental care remains open; this record establishes none of them for any organism other than the family-care migrant and adds nothing to that migrant's own anatomy or behaviour.
Species, names, sizes, proportions, colours, lifespans, and the branch inventory remain open.
Reproduction and care across the lineage remain open; the family-care migrant's care system is its own established behaviour and is not lineage-wide.
Feeding, digestion, senses, respiration, circulation, internal organisation, cognition, sociality, distribution, migration, and disease remain open.
No Lineage V branch other than the family-care migrant is established as present, abundant, or absent at any particular location, including the basin lake.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, universal creature level, spawn mechanism, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Earth life of any era and mythological creatures may inspire author-facing design; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted directly.
Food, oxygen, energy, materials, reproduction, disease, injury, mortality, and carrying capacity remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Water and margin scenes can show genuinely alien radial silhouettes moving by travelling margin waves.
The vaulted brood-carrying migrant reads as the elaborate exception rather than the lineage rule.
Hydrostatic bodies make body-wall breaches, desiccation, and freezing distinctively dangerous.
Every species, branch, local presence, and encounter requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The body plan describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, creature progression rule, spawn source, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What branches exist, and what forms do radial hydrostatic bodies take beyond the vault?
Is any branch fully terrestrial, amphibious, sessile, or colonial?
How do members reproduce and, where applicable, care for young outside the migrant's system?
What feeding, sensory, and respiratory strategies suit a radial hydrostatic body?
Which basin-lake residents, if any, belong to this lineage?
How do hydrostatic bodies handle freezing, desiccation, and wounding across habitats?

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C ancestral-scope cards were presented with A recommended, the Author selected 'A — Radial-hydrostatic core' on 2026-08-17.
